_deal: The board's test node, until he plays it.
author: jessica
source: his 2026-10-23: the military family ("like 10 missionboard missions for Military Dungeons"), "we have droppods, those would be cool", 13:35 "don't limit ourselves by what's there already in my mod, we can add the markers needed later", 13:44 "go for it"
_note: THE MILITARY FAMILY, 9 OF ~10: THE HOLDOUTS.
A few soldiers are still holding part of the site and are out of almost everything. Bring the medical crate from
the door to their position, and the sergeant tells you how long they have been there. The verb is BRING, to people
who are still alive: the warm one of the family, kept short.
Written to the delve marker set (outside entrance, centre, item markers, boss, wounded) on his ruling, so the
lint pool is EMPTY on military sites until the markers are on them (missionboard06a's note says why).
Every word holds at any military site: nothing names the site, the faction or the weather; everything the lines
point at is placed. Pay: med, capped.

place._theme: Military sites; the family's marker set.

prose.name: Hauling: Holdouts on <Planet>
prose.briefing: A handful of soldiers are still holding part of the <Place>. They are out of almost everything.
prose.card: Local Contract. Take the medical crate to the holdouts inside the <Place> on <Planet>. Payment on contract completion.

beats.objective: Collect the medical crate at the <Place>
beats.journal: I found the medical crate by the way in, dropped by somebody who didn't want to come any closer. Now I need to get it to the holdouts deeper inside.
beats.name: Medical Crate

beats.journal: The ones keeping the holdouts pinned at the <Place> are dead. The way to them is open, and I need to bring them the crate.
say: That's the way clear. Go to them.

beats.objective: Bring the crate to the holdouts
beats.journal: A few soldiers were still holding part of the <Place>, out of nearly everything. I broke through and brought them a medical crate.

person.name: Sergeant Ndiaye
hellos: Slowly. We've been shooting at shapes for days.

greeting: A medical crate? What's left of us is holding this corner, and we've been out of dressings for three days.

exchanges.prompt: It's yours. Where do you want it?
reply: Right here. One of mine keeps telling me he's fine. I'll find a way to thank you properly once I've slept.

exchanges.prompt: Three days without dressings. Who's worst off?
reply: The one who keeps saying he's fine. Look at him before you go, if you would. He'll listen to a stranger.

exchanges.prompt: How long have you been holding?
reply: Nine days, if the clock on my sleeve is right. Nobody here trusts the clock.
Because nobody told us to. And because if we leave this corner, they have all of it.

exchanges.prompt: I'll make sure someone hears this corner held.
reply: If you can make someone hear, you're the first. Tell them nine days. Tell them nobody left.

beats._talk: Exchange 0 ends the talk, takes the Medical Crate and sets stage 100. 'Nine days' is fixed on purpose and not the unit's: it is a sleeve clock nobody trusts. A rank in a person's name is allowed (it is not a token). Voice 'Jon Jebus', unused so far.
beats._company: His 2026-10-29 'can we add a field so that the mission will spawn friendlies there too': the holdouts are real now, the UC Marines list support uses (armed, friendly). Untested whether a person's company fights.

broadcast: There's a crate at the entrance. Our people are further in. Get it to them.
_speech: On a board the broadcast waits for him at the site. Not yet heard in game; his ear decides. No names, places, factions or currency in a voiced line.
